tagline: A gentle climb from North Park gives way to the steep Poudre descent.
intro: From the open basin of North Park, Highway 14 climbs gently toward Cameron Pass before descending steeply into the narrow Poudre River valley. The Colorado Department of Transportation includes Cache la Poudre–North Park in its Scenic & Historic Byways program and gives the drive between Walden and Fort Collins as 101 miles and three hours. Its description emphasizes the river canyon and the glaciated mountains and evergreen thickets at Colorado State Forest. Highway 14 is two lanes except for sections near Fort Collins.

Railroad companies surveyed the canyon in the early 1880s, including rivals Union Pacific and Chicago, Burlington and Quincy. No railroad followed; a road was built through the narrows in the 1920s. Baldwin Tunnel began as a single-lane rock tunnel in 1916. It was widened to two lanes in 1951, before the highway’s paving was complete. Highway 14 was fully paved by 1963.

Starting at Walden, follow the route southeast through Gould along the Michigan River valley to Cameron Pass. Beyond the pass, the highway descends beside Joe Wright Creek to Chambers Lake, then follows the Cache la Poudre through its canyon. At Teds Place, it joins US 287 southbound for Fort Collins.

moments.title: Gould
moments.text: Wetlands, pine forest, aspen groves and sagebrush share the valley at Gould, between Owl Mountain and Gould Mountain. Timber shaped the town at the turn of the twentieth century. In 1939, Gould and the Bockman Lumber Camp built simple log cabin schools. In the 1950s, Colorado State Forest headquarters were built on the grounds of a former fish hatchery. The Moose Visitor Center stands on US 14, one mile east of Gould. Gould lies southeast of Walden on Highway 14, in the valley of the Middle Fork of the Michigan River.
moments.notice: Gould’s valley includes wetlands, pine forest, aspen groves and sagebrush.

moments.title: Cameron Pass
moments.text: Cameron Pass occupies a gap between the Medicine Bow and Never Summer mountains at 10,276 feet. Named in 1870 for Robert Cameron, a former Union general and founder of the Fort Collins Agricultural Colony, it drew repeated railroad surveys. Union Pacific considered it for a route through the Rockies, but no railroad crossed the pass. Highway 14 now uses the gap to connect Fort Collins with Walden in North Park. Water drains toward different branches of the Platte: Joe Wright Creek feeds the South Platte basin, while the Michigan River feeds the North Platte.

moments.title: Rustic
moments.text: Rustic stands beside Highway 14 and the Cache la Poudre River. S. B. Stewart built the Rustic Hotel here in 1881; it soon became a summer tourist resort. The town was established the following year. The hotel burned in 2008. Downstream, fishing and hunting resort cabins occur along the canyon, where some cabins are occupied only seasonally.

practical: Cameron Pass: Cameron Pass usually remains open year-round, but receives heavy winter snow and is prone to avalanches. (checked 2026-10-11)
